context.analysis:
## Overview
This system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old mainframe claims platform through a gradual hybrid migration. It replaces legacy components while ensuring continuous claims processing and business continuity.

## Key Elements
* Customers & Brokers: External users submitting claims online
* Claims Adjusters: Internal users managing claims via the new web application
* New Insurance Claims Platform: Azure West Europe cloud-native services including Azure App Service, Azure Functions, and Azure API Management
* Migration Router / Facade: Architectural gateway handling incremental claim type routing and rollback
* Legacy Mainframe: On-premise COBOL/DB2 system of record
* Identity Provider: Corporate Active Directory / Azure AD
* Notification Service: SendGrid/Twilio external SMS/email provider

## Relationships
* Customers, Brokers, and Adjusters interact with the New Insurance Claims Platform via HTTPS/WSS
* New Insurance Claims Platform authenticates against Identity Provider via OpenID Connect/OAuth 2.0
* New Insurance Claims Platform synchronizes data with Legacy Mainframe via Azure Service Bus over Azure ExpressRoute/VPN
* New Insurance Claims Platform integrates with Notification Service via HTTPS REST API

## Technology Stack
* Cloud Platform: Azure West Europe for modern containerized and serverless workloads, addressing team inexperience through managed services
* Integration & Messaging: Azure Service Bus and Azure API Management to protect the legacy mainframe batch window
* Infrastructure & Security: Terraform/Bicep for GitOps, Azure Key Vault for secrets management, and Azure Application Insights for distributed tracing
* Hybrid Connectivity: Azure ExpressRoute or Site-to-Site VPN securing data in transit between cloud and on-premise

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture protects the 3-year mainframe system-of-record constraint while incrementally migrating claim types to the cloud. The Migration Router and asynchronous messaging ensure zero data loss, low adjuster latency, and rapid 1-day rollback capabilities.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a hybrid cloud platform on Azure West Europe, ensuring uninterrupted claims processing for customers, brokers, and adjusters.]

## Key Elements
- Customers [person, context]
- Brokers [person, context]
- Claims Adjuster [person, context]
- New Insurance Claims Platform [system, context] (Azure Cloud)
- Customer Portal SPA [container] (Azure Static Web Apps, React/TypeScript)
- API Gateway [container] (Azure API Management)
- Claims Processing Core & BFF [container] (Azure Kubernetes Service)
- Routing & Reconciliation Service [container] (Azure Kubernetes Service + Azure Cosmos DB)
- Legacy Mainframe [externalSystem, context] (COBOL/DB2, On-Premise)
- Identity Provider [externalSystem, context] (Corporate Active Directory / Azure AD)
- Notification Service [externalSystem, context] (SendGrid/Twilio)

## Relationships
- Customers -> Customer Portal SPA (HTTPS/WSS)
- Brokers -> Customer Portal SPA (HTTPS/WSS)
- Claims Adjuster -> Customer Portal SPA (HTTPS/WSS)
- Customer Portal SPA -> API Gateway (HTTPS REST/GraphQL)
- API Gateway -> Claims Processing Core & BFF (HTTPS / mTLS)
- Claims Processing Core & BFF -> Routing & Reconciliation Service (Internal gRPC/REST)
- Routing & Reconciliation Service -> Legacy Mainframe (Azure Service Bus over Azure ExpressRoute/VPN)
- New Insurance Claims Platform -> Identity Provider (OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0)
- New Insurance Claims Platform -> Notification Service (HTTPS REST API)

## Technology Stack
- Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS): Standardizes backend compute for Claims Processing Core, BFF, and Routing Service to minimize operational overhead for a cloud-inexperienced team.
- Azure API Management (APIM): Enforces rate limiting, OAuth 2.0 token validation, and circuit breaking toward the mainframe.
- Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts the React/TypeScript Customer Portal SPA.
- Azure Cosmos DB: Tracks claims state and reconciliation data for zero-loss guarantees (R-04) and rapid 1-day fallbacks (R-06).
- Azure ExpressRoute / IPSec VPN: Secures hybrid transport between Azure West Europe and the on-premise mainframe.

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates complex claim-type logic within modular AKS services controlled by feature flags, enabling a seamless 1-day fallback to the legacy mainframe without violating strict batch windows or incurring excessive integration costs. Standardizing backend compute on AKS reduces operational complexity for a cloud-beginner team while leveraging managed Azure security and routing services to meet stringent performance and consistency requirements.]

Customer Portal SPA.analysis:
## Overview
This system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurance claims platform by gradually migrating claim types from an on-premise mainframe to a modern Azure cloud environment. It provides a secure online portal for customers and brokers while maintaining legacy system integration for up to three years.

## Key Elements
- Customers
- Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- New Insurance Claims Platform
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2)
- Identity Provider (Active Directory / Azure AD)
- Notification Service (SendGrid/Twilio)
- Customer Portal SPA (Azure Static Web Apps, React/TypeScript)
- API Gateway (Azure API Management)
- Claims Processing Core & BFF (Azure Kubernetes Service)
- Routing & Reconciliation Service (Azure Kubernetes Service + Azure Cosmos DB)

## Relationships
- Customers -> Customer Portal SPA (HTTPS/WSS)
- Brokers -> Customer Portal SPA (HTTPS/WSS)
- Claims Adjusters -> New Insurance Claims Platform (HTTPS/WSS)
- New Insurance Claims Platform -> Identity Provider (OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0)
- New Insurance Claims Platform -> Legacy Mainframe (Azure Service Bus over Azure ExpressRoute/VPN)
- New Insurance Claims Platform -> Notification Service (HTTPS REST API)
- Customer Portal SPA -> API Gateway (HTTPS REST/GraphQL)
- API Gateway -> Claims Processing Core & BFF (HTTPS / mTLS)
- Claims Processing Core & BFF -> Routing & Reconciliation Service (Internal gRPC/REST)
- Routing & Reconciliation Service -> Legacy Mainframe (Azure Service Bus over Azure ExpressRoute/VPN)

## Technology Stack
- Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts the React/TypeScript Customer Portal SPA with global CDN and automated GitHub Actions CI/CD to mitigate low cloud experience.
- Azure API Management: Acts as API Gateway enforcing OAuth 2.0 validation, rate limiting, and circuit breaking.
- Azure Kubernetes Service: Runs Claims Processing Core & BFF and Routing & Reconciliation Service to standardize backend compute.
- Azure Cosmos DB: Stores reconciliation data for zero-loss claims tracking.
- Azure SignalR Service: Manages real-time claim status updates without raw WebSocket operational overhead.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe interactions while gradually migrating workloads to Azure over three years. It ensures zero data loss during migration, maintains sub-two-second adjuster screen performance, and satisfies strict security and maintainability requirements.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurance claims platform by gradually migrating claim types to a hybrid cloud architecture. It replaces legacy components while maintaining uninterrupted processing via an on-premise mainframe system of record.

## Key Elements
- Customers, Brokers, Claims Adjusters
- New Insurance Claims Platform
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2)
- Identity Provider (Active Directory / Azure AD)
- Notification Service (SendGrid/Twilio)
- Customer Portal SPA (Azure Static Web Apps, React/TypeScript)
- API Gateway (Azure API Management)
- Claims Processing Core & BFF (Azure Kubernetes Service)
- Routing & Reconciliation Service (Azure Kubernetes Service + Azure Cosmos DB)

## Relationships
- Customers, Brokers, Claims Adjusters -> New Insurance Claims Platform [HTTPS/WSS]
- New Insurance Claims Platform -> Identity Provider [OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0]
- New Insurance Claims Platform -> Legacy Mainframe [Azure Service Bus over Azure ExpressRoute/VPN]
- New Insurance Claims Platform -> Notification Service [HTTPS REST API]
- Customer Portal SPA -> API Gateway [HTTPS REST/GraphQL]
- API Gateway -> Claims Processing Core & BFF [HTTPS / mTLS]
- Claims Processing Core & BFF -> Routing & Reconciliation Service [Internal gRPC/REST]
- Routing & Reconciliation Service -> Legacy Mainframe [Azure Service Bus over Azure ExpressRoute/VPN]

## Technology Stack
- Azure West Europe: Primary cloud region for scalability and managed services.
- Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS): Hosts backend microservices, optimizing operational efficiency for teams with limited cloud experience.
- Azure API Management (APIM): Enforces rate limiting, JWT validation via JWKS, WAF, and RFC 7807 error mapping.
- Azure Cosmos DB: Manages high-performance claims state and reconciliation data for zero-loss guarantees.
- Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts the React/TypeScript Customer Portal SPA.
- Azure Key Vault: Centralized secret management utilizing managed identities.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture decouples modern web clients from the legacy mainframe, ensuring sub-second adjuster screens and secure single sign-on without overloading fragile on-premise batch windows. Claim types can migrate incrementally while maintaining zero-loss consistency and rapid one-day fallback capabilities.

Routing & Reconciliation Service.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid cloud insurance claims platform designed to gradually modernize a 30-year-old mainframe system over three years. It ensures zero data loss and rapid fallbacks while the legacy system processes ongoing claims.

## Key Elements
- Customers [person]
- Brokers [person]
- Claims Adjusters [person]
- Customer Portal SPA (Azure Static Web Apps, React/TypeScript) [container]
- API Gateway (Azure API Management) [container]
- Claims Processing Core & BFF (Azure Kubernetes Service) [container]
- Routing & Reconciliation Service (Azure Kubernetes Service + Azure Cosmos DB) [container]
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2) [externalSystem]
- Identity Provider (Active Directory / Azure AD) [externalSystem]
- Notification Service (SendGrid/Twilio) [externalSystem]
- Claim Router Component (C#/.NET Core / gRPC) [component]
- Reconciliation Engine Component (C#/.NET Core Worker Service) [component]
- DLQ Manager Component (C#/.NET Core / Azure Service Bus SDK) [component]
- Reconciliation Dashboard API Component (C#/.NET Core / ASP.NET Web API) [component]
- Audit & State Store Component (Azure Cosmos DB, SQL API) [component]

## Relationships
- Customers -> Customer Portal SPA [HTTPS/WSS]
- Brokers -> Customer Portal SPA [HTTPS/WSS]
- Claims Adjusters -> Customer Portal SPA [HTTPS/WSS]
- Customer Portal SPA -> API Gateway [HTTPS REST/GraphQL]
- API Gateway -> Claims Processing Core & BFF [HTTPS / mTLS]
- Claims Processing Core & BFF -> Routing & Reconciliation Service [Internal gRPC/REST]
- Routing & Reconciliation Service -> Legacy Mainframe [Azure Service Bus over Azure ExpressRoute/VPN]
- Customer Portal SPA -> Identity Provider [OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0]
- Claims Processing Core & BFF -> Notification Service [HTTPS REST API]
- Claim Router Component -> Audit & State Store Component [HTTPS / Cosmos DB SQL API]
- Reconciliation Engine Component -> Audit & State Store Component [HTTPS / Cosmos DB SQL API]
- DLQ Manager Component -> Audit & State Store Component [HTTPS / Cosmos DB SQL API]
- Reconciliation Dashboard API Component -> Audit & State Store Component [HTTPS / Cosmos DB SQL API]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS): Hosts backend microservices and containerized components with minimal operational overhead for a cloud-inexperienced team.
- Azure Cosmos DB (SQL API): Persists immutable transaction logs and state data using native SQL APIs to reduce abstraction complexity.
- Azure Service Bus: Manages reliable messaging over Azure ExpressRoute/VPN during strict mainframe batch windows.
- C# / .NET Core: Powers the core components, worker services, and APIs for consistent enterprise development.
- React / TypeScript: Delivers a modern responsive UI within Azure Static Web Apps.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture securely bridges legacy on-premise COBOL/DB2 mainframes with Azure cloud services using robust routing and reconciliation patterns. This ensures regulatory compliance, zero data loss, and rapid one-day rollbacks per claim type.
